text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager: high error rate on inference-serving-prod (eu-west). 502/503 spike at 12:03 UTC — paging @oncall

Sam T: seeing a lot of pod CrashLoopBackOffs in serving-runtime namespace, GPUs OOM logs on restart. autoscaler also ramped nodes up from 40 -> 85 in ~6m

Maya R: confirmed, metrics: token throughput down 35%, 95th latency up ~4x. Affected customer traffic routed to eu-west only.

Pete G: stacktrace from one crashed pod: `CUDA error: out of memory attempting to allocate 2.1GiB` then `container restart` repeatedly. Also lots of `kubelet evicting` events.

Infra SRE: autoscaler saw lots of pending pods (pending due to resource mismatch) and kept adding nodes. New nodes come up with older NVIDIA driver (470.x) while the runtime expects 525.x — that mismatch causes some drivers to allocate more memory and fail.

Sam T: that explains the OOM pattern on start. new nodes = different AMI image in eu-west autoscaling group. seems like a mixed-launch-template update accidentally rolled earlier this morning.

Maya R: customer impact: CS reports 2 enterprise customers saw 15-20% failed requests for ~10m. tagging as P1. CS Liaison pulled initial impact notes.

CS Liaison: reached out to affected customers, they're seeing retries and higher latency; asking for ETA and mitigation steps.

Pete G: immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause cluster-autoscaler (scale-control) 2) cordon/evict pods from bad nodes 3) force image/driver roll on new nodes -> replace with validated AMI 4) throttle incoming traffic / route to eu-central fallback models

Infra SRE: I'm pausing cluster-autoscaler now: `kubectl -n kube-system scale deploy/cluster-autoscaler --replicas=0`

IncidentBot: deploy/cluster-autoscaler scaled to 0 replicas by Infra SRE

Maya R: good. also reduce HPA max replicas on serving-runtime to stop churn: `kubectl patch hpa runtime-hpa -p '{"spec": {"maxReplicas": 60}}'`

Sam T: running cordon on suspect nodes (list from ASG-xxxx): `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-5-123.eu-west.compute.internal` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`

Infra SRE: cordoned 7 nodes. draining. moving pods off to healthy nodes. Might still see transient OOMs while pods restart.

eng-runtime: suggestion — spin up a small cpu-only canary pool and redirect low-priority traffic there, reduce GPU pressure. We can route non-enterprise traffic to cpu-path and keep enterprise on pinned healthy nodes.

CS Liaison: customers ok with short routing changes if it stabilizes SLA. keeping them updated.

Pete G: looking at kube-events, I see repeated `failed to allocate memory` from libtorch init on some model shards, not just driver mismatch. Could be a startup concurrency + large batch size causing KV-cache blowups.

Sam T: patching runtime config to reduce startup batch concurrency: `kubectl set env deploy/runtime --containers=runtime BATCH_CONCURRENCY=1` — doing a rolling restart with `kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime`

Maya R: rolling restart started. watching logs.

~2 minutes later~

eng-runtime: after reducing concurrency, instances are more stable on healthy nodes. fewer immediate OOMs, but autoscaler pause needed until nodes are replaced.

Infra SRE: initiating ASG replace for the bad launch-template version: creating new launch configuration with driver 525. we'll terminate the suspect instances gracefully (drain first). ETA ~8-12m for full replacement.

Sam T: in parallel, I'm lowering HPA target CPU and mem thresholds so we don't overschedule: `kubectl patch hpa runtime-hpa -p '{"spec": {"metrics": [{"type":"Resource","resource":{"name":"cpu","targetAverageUtilization":50}}]}}'`

Oncall Bot: Handing off incident to second on-call in 20m. @Maya R will take next shift if this persists.

Maya R: I'll take handoff at 12:30 UTC. current status: ingress error rate down from peak 18% -> 6%, p95 latency trending down. still seeing ~5 crashloops on older nodes.

Pete G: log snippet from crashed container: ```
[2026-03-15T12:10:45Z] ERROR runtime: GPU memory allocation failed: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-15T12:10:46Z] INFO runtime: restarting process (crashloop)
```

Maya R: good snapshot. CS Liaison, please hold customers to 'mitigated, team working on node replacement and autoscaler adjustments'

CS Liaison: acknowledged, sent update.

Infra SRE: ASG new AMI baked and deployed; starting controlled instance termination of 9 nodes. Drained and terminated 3 so far. New nodes joining with correct driver.

eng-runtime: after 3 terminations, crashloops stopped for pods rescheduled onto new nodes. we should keep autoscaler disabled until all bad nodes replaced and HPA limits relaxed.

Sam T: we should also add a cooldown to cluster-autoscaler config and pin launch template to avoid implicit mixed-template rotations. Follow-up TODOs: 1) add ASG invariant check in deployment pipeline 2) add preflight that verifies driver versions match runtime 3) circuit-breaker in autoscaler for rapid up/down (rate limiting) 4) run a chaos test for node-driver mismatch

Maya R: agreed. raising a follow-up ticket for infra and runtime to own fixes. I'll include customer impact notes and timeline.

Oncall Bot: Handoff time. @Maya R is now the active on-call. Incident state: mitigation in progress, autoscaler paused, node replacement underway.

Maya R: taking it. current ask: monitor for any residual 502s and watch eu-west ingress qps. I'll keep CS updated, and if anything re-spikes we re-open full pager.

IncidentBot: note: incident will be marked as P1 until all affected customers confirmed stable or 60m elapsed.

CS Liaison: will keep the customers posted every 15m. next update in ~10m.

Sam T: quick checklist for runbook: - autoscaler paused - bad nodes cordoned/drained - AMI rollout in progress - HPA max lowered - batch concurrency reduced - cpu fallback routing enabled - CS notified

Maya R: thanks team. leaving a pinned snippet of commands used for postmortem runbook.

Sam T: posted the commands to the incidents docs page and created the follow-up ticket IR-2026-014.

Pete G: final note before handoff: we should consider adding a startup memory probe to the runtime that fails the readiness check when initial GPU alloc > X GiB — prevents pod from being scheduled until it's safe.

Maya R: noted. handoff complete.

IncidentBot: Incident thread closed for active pager handoff (still open as mitigated). Refer to IR-2026-014 for postmortem actions.
